overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that space and planetary anomalies dominate traction, specifically extreme 'What If' hypothetical scenarios combined with bizarre cosmic facts (e.g., TrES-2b, liquid diamond planets, and burning ice worlds). Videos incorporating high-stakes spatial comparisons or impossible planetary environments consistently achieve higher views-per-day and stronger engagement rates (likes/comments per view) compared to abstract psychological tricks or older historical topics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generate over 900-1000+ views rapidly with high like counts relative to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical immersion formats where the viewer is placed directly into an impossible, hazardous cosmic environment.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) outperform standard science explainers by leveraging visceral, counter-intuitive visual descriptors.
winning_patterns.action: Continue pairing rare planetary weather phenomena or extreme material properties with punchy, high-curiosity titles.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics covering songs stuck in your head (ef3ND4qiRHc, Jc04LVKNd2s) and basic memory glitches stall out under 100 views with zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize minor cognitive tips and earworm mechanics unless reframed into a high-stakes neurological thriller format.

weak_patterns.evidence: Aged or overly niche historical mysteries (yLm-FjYH6-k) stagnate compared to dynamic, visual space-time anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Shift historical storytelling content toward high-drama micro-stories or cosmic-scale historical comparisons rather than static artifact facts.

next_video.concept: What happens to your body if you accidentally stepped onto a rogue planet drifting through interstellar space with zero sunlight?
next_video.opening_direction: Start with an immediate, jarring sensory premise: Imagine stepping outside where the temperature is absolute zero and the stars are completely gone.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that without a star, the planet's core is still active, creating glowing rivers of liquid nitrogen that freeze your breath instantly mid-air.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' format and planetary anomaly niche while introducing a completely fresh celestial subject (rogue planets and liquid nitrogen rivers) distinct from previous diamond or iron rain topics.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use diamond, glass, ruby, or iron rain themes.
Do not reuse TrES-2b or J1407b.
Must feature a completely new celestial body type (rogue planet / interstellar wanderer).

experiment: A/B test a pure planetary fact title ('The Rogue Planet Traveling Alone Through the Void') against an immersive 'What If' title ('What If You Landed on a Planet With No Sun?') to see which drives higher retention in the critical first 3 seconds.
